deep.reconstruction:
The page has two unrelated parts.

PART A (top). This continues the previous page, where Riemann expands, in powers of 1/alpha, an operator acting on f(s). The terms there involve f^{(3n-2k)}(s)/(n! 6^n 2^{3n} (pi i)^n). Those are the coefficient computations for the asymptotic (Riemann–Siegel type) correction terms.

(1) Recurrence. Write a^m_n for the coefficient at level n and index m. The recurrence is
  a^m_n + pi*i*a^{m-1}_{n-1} - (3n-2-4m)(3n-1-4m)/(16 pi i) * a^m_{n-1} = 0.

(2) Normalization. Note that (3n-2-4m)(3n-1-4m)/16 = (9/16)(n-4m/3-2/3)(n-4m/3-1/3). Riemann sets
  c^m_n = a^m_n (16 pi i/9)^n / [Pi(n-4m/3-2/3) Pi(n-4m/3-1/3)],
with Pi(x) = Gamma(x+1). Using Pi(x) = x Pi(x-1), the three-term recurrence becomes a first-order difference equation in n:
  c^m_n - c^m_{n-1} = -pi*i*a^{m-1}_{n-1} (16 pi i/9)^n / [Pi(n-4m/3-1/3) Pi(n-4m/3-2/3)].
Shifting m -> m-1 and n -> n-1 in the definition gives
  c^{m-1}_{n-1} = a^{m-1}_{n-1} (16 pi i/9)^{n-1} / [Pi(n-4m/3) Pi(n-4m/3-1/3)],
which agrees with what is written. Substituting this, my own computation gives
  c^m_n - c^m_{n-1} = -pi*i*(16 pi i/9) c^{m-1}_{n-1} Pi(n-4m/3)/Pi(n-4m/3-2/3).
Riemann (as transcribed) writes the denominator as Pi(n-4m/3-1/3).

(3) Solving level by level.
- m=0: c^0_n is constant, since the a^{-1} terms vanish.
- m=1: the increment is Const * Pi(n-4/3)/Pi(n-5/3), which is the m=1 case of his formula. He labels it c^1_n, but it is really the increment c^1_n - c^1_{n-1}.
- To sum such Gamma ratios over n, he writes them as Euler Beta integrals, e.g. int_0^1 (1-x)^{2/3} x^{n-4m/3} dx and int (1-x)^{-1/3} x^{n-4m/3} dx. The sum over n then becomes a geometric series under the integral sign.
- m=2: a tentative form Const * Pi(n-4/3)Pi(n-8/3)/(Pi(n-2/3)Pi(n-2)), with Beta-type integrals (1-x)^{5/3} x^{n-4/3} and (1-x)^{-8/3} x^{n-4/3}.
- An iterated integral int (1-x)^{-5/3} x^{-2/3} int x^{n-2/3}/(1-x) dx dx, which represents the double sum.
The work breaks off there. The goal is a closed form for c^m_n, hence for the coefficients of the correction terms.

PART B (bottom). This is the functional equation of the Dirichlet L-series mod 4, which Riemann calls chi(s) (modern L(s,chi_4) = beta(s)).

(1) Euler product and series:
  chi(s) = prod_p 1/(1 - (-1)^{(p-1)/2} p^{-s}) = sum_{m odd} (-1)^{(m-1)/2} m^{-s} = sum_n (-1)^n (2n+1)^{-s}.

(2) Mellin integral. From n^{-s} Pi(s-1) = int_0^oo e^{-nx} x^{s-1} dx, summing gives
  Pi(s-1) chi(s) = int_0^oo x^{s-1} sum (-1)^n e^{-(2n+1)x} dx = int_0^oo x^{s-1} e^{-x}/(1+e^{-2x}) dx.

(3) Hankel loop and residues. He turns this into a loop integral (written int_oo^oo), which brings in the factor sin(pi s). He then shifts the contour and collects residues at 2x = ±(2m+1) pi i. There e^{-x}/(1+e^{-2x}) has residues ±(1/2)e^{∓(m+1/2)pi i}-type values, and the margin notes evaluate the phases.

(4) Collecting terms. The residues combine into
  sum (-1)^m (2m+1)^{s-1} (pi/2)^s * const * cos(pi s/2).
The margin note (i^s + i^{-s}) gives 2cos(pi s/2). He obtains
  sin(pi s) Pi(s-1) chi(s) = (pi/2)^s * 4 cos(pi s/2) * chi(1-s).

(5) Symmetric form. He uses:
- Legendre duplication: sqrt(pi) Pi(s-1) = 2^{s-1} Pi((s-1)/2) Pi(s/2-1);
- the reflection formula: Pi(s/2-1) Pi(-s/2) = pi/sin(pi s/2);
- sin(pi s) = 2 sin(pi s/2) cos(pi s/2).
This gives
  Pi((s-1)/2) chi(s) 2^{s-1} pi^{-1/2} = 2 (pi/2)^s chi(1-s) Pi(-s/2)/pi.
The manuscript writes chi(s-1) here, meaning chi(1-s). Finally:
  Pi((s-1)/2) chi(s) (pi/4)^{-s/2} = Pi(-s/2) chi(1-s) (pi/4)^{(s-1)/2}.
This is invariant under s -> 1-s. In modern form it is Lambda(s) = (pi/4)^{-(s+1)/2} Gamma((s+1)/2) beta(s) = Lambda(1-s).

This is exactly the method of his 1859 zeta paper, transferred to the character mod 4.
errors: Part A: substituting c^{m-1}_{n-1} into the difference equation should give the ratio Pi(n-4m/3)/Pi(n-4m/3-2/3). The page (as transcribed) has Pi(n-4m/3-1/3) in the denominator. Either this is a slip or the image reading is uncertain; the later m=1 expression Pi(n-4/3)/Pi(n-5/3) follows the written (-1/3) version.
Part A: 'c^1_n = Const. Pi(n-4/3)/Pi(n-5/3)' is the increment c^1_n - c^1_{n-1}, not c^1_n itself. Summing it gives a ratio of the type Pi(n-1/3)/Pi(n-5/3).

Part B: the residue/collection step has a factor-2 error. The correct relation is sin(pi s) Gamma(s) beta(s) = 2 (pi/2)^s cos(pi s/2) beta(1-s), not 4. Check at s->0: the left side is pi*beta(0) = pi/2, while the right side with 4 gives pi.
Part B: the same factor 2 carries into the line Pi((s-1)/2)chi(s)2^{s-1}pi^{-1/2} = 2(pi/2)^s chi(1-s)Pi(-s/2)/pi. The leading 2 should be 1.
Part B: the final symmetric line silently drops this factor 2 and is correct. The two slips compensate, so the end result is right.
Part B: chi(s-1) is written where chi(1-s) is meant, in the second-to-last line (and in the transcription of the final line).
Part B: the integrand should be e^{-x}/(e^{-2x}+1), equivalently 1/(e^x+e^{-x}). As transcribed, e^{-x}/(e^{2x}+1) is wrong; the image shows a correction in the denominator.

results.what: Three-term recurrence for the coefficients a^m_n of the asymptotic correction terms, reduced by Gamma-function normalization to a first-order difference equation and summed via Euler Beta integrals
results.modern_name: Computation of the coefficients of the higher correction terms in the Riemann–Siegel asymptotic formula (cf. later work of Gabcke)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's Nachlass as reported by Siegel (1932); systematic coefficient recursions later by Gabcke (1979)

results.what: Euler product and Dirichlet series for L(s,chi_4) and its Mellin integral representation Gamma(s)beta(s) = int_0^oo x^{s-1}/(e^x+e^{-x}) dx
results.modern_name: Dirichlet beta function / L-function mod 4, Mellin transform

results.what: Functional equation of L(s,chi_4) by Hankel contour and residues, put into the symmetric Gamma-completed form
results.modern_name: Functional equation of the Dirichlet beta function: Lambda(s) = (pi/4)^{-(s+1)/2} Gamma((s+1)/2) beta(s) = Lambda(1-s)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (stated 1749), proved by Malmsten (1849) and Schlömilch; general case Hurwitz (1882)

deep.surprise_reason: The functional equation for beta(s) predates Riemann (Euler, Malmsten). His contour method is the obvious transfer of his 1859 zeta argument, and the symmetric Gamma-completed form is natural in his hands; the result is a minor unpublished detail. The coefficient recurrence belongs to the Riemann–Siegel material, which is already known from Siegel's 1932 study of the Nachlass, though this specific normalization and Beta-integral summation may be undocumented.

transcription_corrections: Integrand in the Mellin line should read e^{-x}/(e^{-2x}+1) (the denominator in the image is corrected); 'e^{-x}/(e^{2x}+1)' is mathematically wrong.
'chi(s-1)' in the last two lines stands for chi(1-s); the image itself appears to show chi(s-1), so this is likely Riemann's own notational slip.
'int_infty^infty' denotes the Hankel loop integral (from +infinity around 0 back to +infinity).
In the residue line the second exponential is likely e^{+3(m+1/2) pi i} rather than e^{+(3m+1/2) pi i}.
'c^1_n = Const. Pi(n-4/3)/Pi(n-5/3)' should be read as the increment c^1_n - c^1_{n-1}.
The denominator in the second line of the c-difference may be Pi(n-4m/3-1/3) as transcribed, but the derivation requires -2/3; recheck the image.
